senses.gloss:
Tauvilikā, occurring once in a hymn of the Atharvaveda,^1
is a word of quite uncertain sense. Roth^2 thinks it means
some kind of beast; Zimmer^3 and Whitney^4 regard it as a
sort of plant; Sāyaṇa explains it as a disease-causing demon,
while Bloomfield^5 leaves the sense doubtful.
1) vi. 16, 3.
2) St. Petersburg Dictionary, s.v.
3) Altindisches Leben, 72.
4) Translation of the Atharvaveda,
292.
5) Hymns of the Atharvaveda, 30, 466.
